newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-LAJUNEN LEADS NORDIC COMBINED AFTER SKI JUMPING.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-LAJUNEN LEADS NORDIC COMBINED AFTER SKI JUMPING.

text.p: Finn Samppa Lajunen took the lead in the Nordic combined event of the Nordic skiing world championships after Saturday's ski jumping but he was under threat from Japanese Kenji Ogiwara.
A first effort of 90.5 metres and a second one of 90 metres allowed Lajunen to go top before Sunday's second part of the competition, the 15-km freestyle cross-country race.
But the experienced Ogiwara, the 1993 world champion, was a close second with jumps of 87.5 and 90 metres.
Lajunen had 234.5 points compared to Ogiwara's 232. German Jens Deimel, more at ease in ski jumping than in cross country, was third on 227.5 points.

The thousands of fans lining the 90-metre hill despite cold winds and light snowfalls went crazy when Norway's Bjarte Engen Vik jumped 96 metres, the day's best mark, at his second attempt to climb to fourth place in the provisional standings.
Vik was a modest 24th after an unimpressive first jump of 81.5 metres.

His performance made up for a disappointing showing by compatriot Fred Boerre Lundberg, the reigning world champion. Lundberg excels in cross country but he lost almost all hope of a medal by ending the first day in 33rd position.
